title: Automation Coverage — Testver QA
subtitle: Test-management cases + Test Explorer script library · as of 19 Nov 2026

summary.verdict: Coverage exists on paper (100% of requirements have cases) but automation is thin where it matters: only 3% of critical-priority cases are automated and 33 of 57 scripts have never run.

findings.title: Critical-priority automation is 1 of 32 cases (3%).
findings.detail: High is 31/57 (54%) and medium 24/34 (71%) — the riskiest tier is the least automated (testver get_automation_stats).

findings.title: 33 of 57 scripts (57.9%) have never run.
findings.detail: Only 13 are passing and 11 failing on their last run; every never-run script is effectively untested (test_library summary).

findings.title: 28 of 57 scripts (49%) are not linked to any test case.
findings.detail: 67 of 123 cases have no script mapped, so platform coverage under-reports the automation that actually exists (test_library vs get_automation_stats).

findings.title: 11 scripts fail on their last run — all on 30s timeouts.
findings.detail: 5 in tests/admin, 6 in tests/auth (profile 2FA + settings); the whole admin module has no passing script (test_library failing set).

findings.title: Requirements are fully covered by cases, not by automation.
findings.detail: 20/20 requirements and 3/3 sources covered, but automation coverage of cases is 46% — regression is still largely manual (get_coverage_stats).

method: Sources: testver get_automation_stats and get_coverage_stats (test-case side: 123 total cases / 122 in coverage stats, 56 vs 55 automated — the two endpoints disagree by one case, figures shown use get_automation_stats); testver query_requirements (20 active requirements); test_library summary (all 57 Playwright scripts in 14 files, status = each script's LAST run, never_run = no run recorded, flaky overlaps the status buckets); automation_report summary since 90d (63 finished runs, verification re-runs excluded) for executed-run context. Automation coverage = automated test cases ÷ total test cases. Script-link coverage = scripts linked to a test case ÷ 57. No target thresholds are stored in the platform, so status flags reflect priority-risk, not a formal gate.

cells.content:
## Where the coverage gap actually is
- **Critical tier:** 31 of 32 critical-priority cases are still manual — REQ-19 (RBI tokenization / PII), REQ-15, REQ-9 and REQ-6 are the requirement-level names to attack first.
- **Never-run scripts (33):** concentrated in `tests/forms` (6/6), `tests/dynamic` (5/5), `tests/state` (4/4), `tests/elements` (2/2) and `tests/modules` (1/1) — these folders contribute **zero** verified automation today.
- **Admin module:** 5 scripts, 5 failing (all 30s timeouts) — the module has no green script, so its 5 linked cases (TC-42 – TC-46) are coverage on paper only.
- **Linking debt:** 28 scripts carry no test case and 67 of 123 cases carry no script; either direction of linking closes the reporting gap.
- **Run context (automation_report, since 90d):** 63 finished runs, 168 executed tests, 79.2% test-level pass rate (avg run pass rate 67%), 14 verification re-runs excluded.
